Unit 1 of 10: How I Taught My Grandmother to Read: The Story

Key ideas

  • Author: Sudha Murty. The narrator is a twelve-year-old girl living with her grandmother Krishtakka in a village in north Karnataka.
  • Transport is poor: newspapers and the weekly magazine arrive late, carried by the bus.
  • The Kannada weekly Karmaveera carries a serial novel, Kashi Yatre by Triveni. The narrator reads each episode aloud; Krishtakka listens closely, remembers it, and discusses it with her friends at the temple.
  • Krishtakka feels close to the old woman in the novel who longs to go to Kashi (Varanasi).
  • The narrator goes away for a week to a wedding. The magazine arrives, and Krishtakka, who never went to school, cannot read it. She feels helpless and cries.
  • At sixty-two, she decides to learn the Kannada alphabet, with Saraswati Puja during Dassara as her deadline. Her granddaughter becomes her teacher.
  • On Dassara, Krishtakka gives her granddaughter a gift, touches her feet as a teacher, and reads the title of Kashi Yatre aloud.

Worked examples

Example 1: Why did Krishtakka cry when the magazine arrived? Answer: her granddaughter was away, and as she could not read, she could not follow the story she loved; she felt helpless and dependent on others.

Example 2: What deadline did she set herself? Answer: to read on her own by Saraswati Puja during Dassara.

10-mark practice set

  1. (1 mark, MCQ) The serial Kashi Yatre was written by: (a) Sudha Murty (b) Triveni (c) Krishtakka (d) R. K. Narayan. Answer: (b).
  2. (1 mark) How old was Krishtakka when she decided to learn to read? Answer: sixty-two.
  3. (2 marks) Why did the family wait eagerly for the bus every day? Answer: the bus brought newspapers, magazines and post to the village (1); there was no other quick link to the outside world (1).
  4. (3 marks) Describe what happened when the narrator went away to a wedding. (40–50 words) Answer: the magazine arrived while she was away (1); Krishtakka could not read the new episode and felt helpless (1); she was too embarrassed to ask others and decided to learn to read herself (1).
  5. (3 marks) How did Krishtakka show respect to her teacher at the end? Answer: she gave her granddaughter a gift on Saraswati Puja (1); she touched her feet, as one does to honour a teacher (1); this showed that she valued learning more than age or status (1).

Common mistakes

  1. Calling the narrator a boy. 2. Saying Krishtakka learnt Hindi. 3. Confusing the novel's author with the chapter's author. 4. Forgetting why she touched her granddaughter's feet. 5. Giving the wrong festival.

Quick recall

  1. Author? 2. Grandmother's name? 3. Magazine? 4. Serial? 5. Deadline festival?

Answers: 1) Sudha Murty. 2) Krishtakka. 3) Karmaveera. 4) Kashi Yatre. 5) Dassara (Saraswati Puja).
